(a) In evaluating any offer deemed a candidate for a Superior Proposal, the Board shall not rely solely on the financial point of view. (c) In situations where the adjustments in the offer's financial aspects are offset by significant improvements in corporate governance or a long-term sustainability roadmap, the Board shall integrate these additional parameters into its evaluation to ensure that the financial point of view is not isolated from the broader corporate strategy.

(b) Should there be any material amendment to the Acquisition Proposal after the initial evaluation period, the Board must re-assess the proposal by integrating both financial and non-financial factors without any one factor, including the financial point of view, being considered in isolation. (c) It is expressly agreed by the parties that the assessment of the superiority of any offer is a composite evaluation where no single factor, even if numerically attractive, shall exclusively drive the decision.
